quote: Hermes is MIT-licensed, model-agnostic and self-hosted, reachable through Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal or email, with persistent memory, self-written skills and a built-in scheduler. It is excellent, and it gave me the same magical feeling I had when I first set up OpenClaw. But it's definitely also a developer's tool, and most knowledge workers will find the setup intimidating.
author: Christian Pean
notes: Surgeon: Hermes excellent/OpenClaw-magic feel but developer-tool setup barrier.

quote: Running Opus 5.5 with a 1M window through a Claude subscription plugin in Hermes Agent burned the limit by lunch, because every turn re-read about 800K tokens of old chat. The fix: compress early and per model.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 27 Clauday: Hermes+Claude 1M re-read ~800K tokens/turn, burned limit by lunch.

quote: Raft is a Slack where humans and AI agents clock in together, and the team open-sourced the whole thing: server, web, CLI, the agent daemon and desktop app. Each agent has a name, role and memory stored locally; they claim tasks, hand off and review each other. Claude Code, Codex and Hermes can join a channel on your own subscription.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 27 Clauday: Raft open-source Slack-with-agents; Hermes can join.

quote: A solo founder says they are officially off the terminal and local development: a Claude-native workflow now hands back completed tasks backed by full end-to-end QA and verification. They tried the same idea early in the year with OpenClaw and Hermes and found it hacky; now it runs across code, design, marketing and support from anywhere.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 28 Clauday: early OpenClaw/Hermes hacky vs Claude-native now.

quote: Hermes takes the opposite posture openly. It is designed to work unattended between check-ins; that is the product, not an oversight. The question is not whether it will act without asking but where you have decided it must stop, and that decision has to be made before it touches real work rather than after.
author: Michael Brandt
notes: Yardwork: Hermes designed for unattended work; autonomy is the product.

quote: Bot Mode, on by default in the desktop app since August 31, turns Hermes profiles into named bots, each with its own model, memory, skills and routines… 250,000+ GitHub stars on September 30.
author: berkkalelioglu

quote: OpenClaw stronger for chat channels/multi-agent/skill library; Hermes stronger for learning/memory/safer defaults.
author: floriangray

quote: Writing a clear rule into a persona file is not the same as enforcing it; move enforcement to code before the model gets a turn.
author: rello1
notes: DEV: persona rules vs code enforcement lesson.

quote: Hermes Agent is a free, MIT licensed AI agent from Nous Research. It runs on your computer or a server, keeps memory between sessions, writes its own skills, and answers from a terminal or from Telegram, Slack and Discord.
author: mdchaitanya
notes: Munder Difflin Oct 3 explainer: Hermes is free MIT-licensed self-hosted agent.

quote: Pick Hermes Agent if you want memory and skills that grow, and a server to keep it on.
author: mdchaitanya
notes: Munder Difflin: Hermes for memory/skills growth with a server.

quote: An always-on agent with a shell is a colleague with root, one who never sleeps, reads everything you point it at, and will cheerfully print a secret to a log if nothing stops it. Security for that colleague is mostly about two questions: what can it reach, and what can it print.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura Oct 1: security framing for always-on shell agents.

quote: I run Hermes Agent in production on my own VPS. Every incident below actually happened to me. Every control below I checked in the source, not the marketing page.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura: production Hermes incidents verified against source.

quote: The agent should never hold a token it could print. The pattern that works is a proxy that holds the credential and a config that only ever points the agent at the proxy.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura: proxy pattern to keep credentials away from agents.

quote: Nous Research issued three sequential releases that archive reviewed project-management inputs as immutable sha256 objects. The approach prevents accidental edits during agent development cycles. Scripts manage the archive process to keep assets stable for repeated runs.
author: amyreed
notes: My AI Guide Oct 5: Hermes pinned inputs as sha256 for reproducibility.

quote: Two of the three most-starred software repositories on GitHub are agent harnesses, OpenClaw at 391,435 stars and Hermes Agent at 251,404, both read from the GitHub API on 5 October 2026.
author: ivantarin
notes: TechThoughtLeaders Oct 5: Hermes Agent 251k stars, #2 agent harness.

quote: Metis' AI agent platform ClawUp now lets anyone deploy their own AI agent in seconds from clawup.org. Users pick a runtime — OpenClaw (the default) or Hermes Agent — choose a model, and hit deploy, with no servers or setup; agents are provisioned in roughly 1–3 minutes.
author: metis
notes: ClawUp Oct 2: one-click Hermes deploy alongside OpenClaw.
